Decor

day-KOR — stress on second syllable · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Decor is the furniture, colors, and decorations used to style the inside of a room or building.

The cafe's decor mixed old travel posters with mismatched armchairs.

Worked Example

The restaurant owner hung mismatched chandeliers, painted the walls deep burgundy, arranged vintage couches, scattered colorful rugs, and displayed old travel posters until the whole space felt like a cozy, bohemian retreat.

Decor is precise here because it captures the entire intentional styling of the space — the colors, furniture, and decorative objects chosen together to create a particular mood. Using only 'furniture' would miss the colors and decorations; 'style' is too vague about specific material elements.

How Decor Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

furnishings

furnishings: the furniture and fittings of a room

style

style: a distinctive, chosen manner or look

design

design: the overall plan for how a space will look; decor is the actual furniture, colors, and ornaments that carry the plan out

Antonyms

austerity

austerity: stark plainness, with nothing decorative added

bareness

bareness: the state of being empty and unfurnished

How Strong Is It? — clutter → arrangement → splendor → decor

clutter vs. decor

clutter vs. decor: Clutter sits at the bottom, far below decor: clutter is a careless mess of objects, while decor is a deliberate, styled selection of furnishings.

arrangement vs. decor

arrangement vs. decor: An arrangement is simply things placed in order, but decor goes further, coordinating furniture, colors, and decorations into one intentional look.

splendor vs. decor

splendor vs. decor: Splendor outshines ordinary decor: decor is the styled look of a room, while splendor is decoration so magnificent it takes your breath away.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — decor

Root — decor: ornament, grace, beauty (from decus, decoris) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: The Latin root decus means 'ornament' or 'grace,' so decor is literally the ornament of a space — the furniture, colors, and decorations that give a room its style.

Use the root in a new word: decorate

Use the root in a new word: decorate: When you decorate a room, you are creating its decor — both words come from Latin decus, meaning 'ornament' or 'grace.'

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / formal

Decor is the precise term when discussing the coordinated styling of an interior — the furniture, colors, and decorations chosen together. Use it when emphasizing the overall aesthetic effect. For individual items alone, 'decoration' works; for furniture only, 'furnishings' is better.
